sections.heading: What Is Extract Text?
sections.body: Extract Text reads the text objects already present in a PDF and writes them to a plain text download for reuse. It does not redesign layout into Word; it prioritizes getting the words out for notes, indexing, or pasting elsewhere quickly. Image-only scans need OCR before meaningful text exists under the page image to extract at all into that downloadable file.

sections.heading: How to Use Extract Text
sections.body: Upload a text-based PDF, extract locally in your browser, and download the .txt file. For scans, run OCR first so real characters exist under the page image.

sections.heading: Why Use Extract Text?
sections.body: Researchers, support teams, and students often need the words without the full layout chrome of the PDF. A one-click text dump beats manual copying across dozens of pages in a viewer. Keeping extraction in the browser avoids uploading confidential PDFs just to grab a few paragraphs for a ticket, outline, or email draft.

sections.heading: Tips for Getting the Best Results
sections.body: If the output is blank or gibberish, the file may be a scan or use unusual encoding—try OCR next. Columns can appear out of reading order in plain text; expect light cleanup in your editor. For tables you plan to calculate on, PDF to Excel is usually a better next step than a raw text dump from Extract Text alone.

faqs.q: Why is my extracted text empty?
faqs.a: The PDF is likely image-only. Run OCR PDF to add a text layer, then extract again.

faqs.q: Does Extract Text keep my file private?
faqs.a: Extraction is designed to run in your browser, so the PDF stays on your device for this tool.

faqs.q: Will formatting and columns be perfect?
faqs.a: Plain text will not preserve complex layout. You get the words; spacing and order may need cleanup.

faqs.q: Can I ask questions about the text afterward?
faqs.a: Yes. Summarize & Ask PDF builds a local extractive summary and keyword answers from the document text.

/extract-text.conclusion: Extract Text turns a PDF’s selectable content into a simple .txt download you can paste or index anywhere. Use it free in your browser on PDF Palette, and run OCR first whenever you are starting from a scan instead of a born-digital file with real text.
